item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00155","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C13","C10","C25"],"selected_candidate_label":"C13","confidence":0.95,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C13 plausibly supplied a material revocation template. Both proclamations identify an earlier proclamation and its statutory basis, explain that a later legal arrangement has displaced the earlier machinery, and conclude by revoking the identified proclamation. They also share the distinctive operative formulation “do hereby revoke the aforesaid [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE].” C10 and C25 are close termination precedents, but they merely end temporary copyright extensions after finding that further time is unnecessary; their operative language and legal transition are less closely aligned with the child.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Whereas the United States has entered into an international agreement... [which] grants specific powers and privileges... with respect to the jurisdiction over offenses committed by members of their armed forces","parent_excerpt":"Whereas the act entitled... approved by me this date, authorizes the Panama Canal Company... and provides that the existing rates of tolls shall continue in effect until changed as provided for therein","explanation":"Each supplies a recital explaining that a new legal regime has replaced the function served by the earlier proclamation."},{"child_excerpt":"do find and declare that the powers and privileges provided in that act... are no longer necessary...; and I hereby revoke the aforesaid [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE]","parent_excerpt":"do hereby revoke the aforesaid [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of March 26, 1948, as modified by the said Proclamations","explanation":"The operative provisions use nearly identical, specific revocation language directed at a previously identified proclamation."},{"child_excerpt":"Whereas under the authority vested in him by section 6 of the act of June 30, 1944... the President... by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE]... extended the powers and privileges provided in that act","parent_excerpt":"Whereas certain changes... were prescribed by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE]... under the authority of section 411 of title 2 of the Canal Zone Code","explanation":"Both begin by identifying the earlier proclamation, the authority under which it was issued, and the legal effect it created before explaining why revocation is warranted."}]}
